title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Opinions on Further Strengthening the Work of Civil Service of Process
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Several Opinions on Further Strengthening Civil Service of Process"

Fa Fa [2017] No. 19

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The "Several Opinions on Further Strengthening Civil Service of Process" are hereby issued to you for implementation.

July 19, 2017

Several Opinions on Further Strengthening Civil Service of Process

Service of process is an important procedural matter in the trial of civil cases, and it is the foundation for ensuring that the people's courts try civil cases fairly and lawfully and timely protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties. In recent years, with the development of China's social economy and the increase in the people's judicial needs, the issue of service of process has become one of the bottlenecks restricting the fairness and efficiency of civil trials. Therefore, people's courts at all levels should effectively improve and strengthen service of process, innovate working mechanisms and methods within the framework of laws and judicial interpretations, comprehensively promote the system for parties to confirm the address for service, unify the format of the confirmation letter for service address, standardize the content of the confirmation letter for service address, enhance the quality and efficiency of civil service of process, and truly implement judicial service for the people.

1. The confirmation letter for service address is the foundation of the system for parties to confirm the address for service. The confirmation letter for service address shall include the service address provided by the party, the matters notified by the people's court, the party's confirmation of the service address, and the scope of application and method of change of the service address.

2. The service address provided by the party shall include the postal code, detailed address, and contact telephone number of the person on whom service is to be made, among others. If electronic service is consented to, the fax number, email address, WeChat account number, or other electronic service address for receiving civil litigation documents shall be provided and confirmed. If a party entrusts an agent ad litem, the service address confirmed by the agent ad litem shall be deemed to be the party's service address.

3. To protect the litigation rights of the parties, the people's court shall inform them of the requirements and precautions for filling in the confirmation letter for service address, as well as the legal consequences of refusing to provide a service address, providing a false address, or providing an inaccurate address.

4. The people's court shall require the party to confirm the matters such as the service address filled in by the party and the legal consequences. The confirmation by the party shall include that the party has been informed of the matters notified by the people's court and the legal consequences of the confirmation letter for service address, warrants that the service address is accurate and valid, and consents to the people's court serving litigation documents through the address confirmed by the party, and shall be signed, sealed, or fingerprinted by the party or the agent ad litem.

5. The people's court shall require the party to confirm the service address at the time of registration and case filing. If the party refuses to confirm the service address, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Registration and Case Filing."

6. The service address confirmed by the party in the confirmation letter for service address shall apply to the first instance proceedings, second instance proceedings, and enforcement proceedings. If the party changes the service address, the party shall notify the people's court in writing. If the party fails to make a written change, the address confirmed by the party shall be the service address.

7. If, due to the inaccuracy of the service address provided by the party, the party's refusal to provide a service address, or the party's failure to notify the people's court in writing of a change of service address, the civil litigation document is not actually received by the person on whom service is to be made, if service is made by personal delivery, the date on which the civil litigation document is left at such address shall be the date of service; if service is made by mail, the date on which the document is returned shall be the date of service.

8. If a party refuses to confirm the service address or evades or avoids service by refusing to respond to the lawsuit, refusing to answer phone calls, avoiding service personnel, moving away from the original residence, or other means, and the people's court cannot or is unable to require the party to confirm the service address, the matter may be handled in the following circumstances, respectively:

(1) If the parties have explicitly agreed on a service address in the contract or correspondence involved in the lawsuit, the agreed address shall be the service address;

(2) If there is no such agreement, the address of the party set forth in the written materials submitted by the party in the lawsuit shall be the service address;

(3) If there is no agreement and the party has not submitted written materials or the written materials do not set forth an address, the address provided in other litigation or arbitration cases within the past year shall be the service address;

(4) If none of the above circumstances exist, the address frequently used by the party in civil activities within the past year shall be the service address.

When serving in accordance with the above addresses, the people's court may simultaneously notify the person on whom service is to be made by telephone, WeChat, or other means.

9. If the service address still cannot be confirmed in accordance with Article 8, the service address for a natural person shall be the domicile registered in the household registration or the address registered in the place of habitual residence; for a legal person or other organization, the service address shall be the domicile registered with the industry and commerce administration or other legally registered or filed domicile.

10. On the premise of strictly abiding by the Civil Procedure Law and the judicial interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law regarding the conditions for application of electronic service, proactive efforts shall be made to explore effective methods and approaches for electronic service and preservation of service evidence. Courts with the necessary conditions may establish a dedicated electronic service platform, or rely on the litigation service platform for electronic service, or cooperate with large portal websites and communication operators to effect service through dedicated email addresses, specific communication numbers, information public accounts, or other means.

11. Where service is made by fax or email, the service personnel shall record the fax sending and receiving numbers, the email sending and receiving addresses, the sending time, and the name of the served litigation document, and print the fax sending confirmation sheet or the webpage showing successful email sending, and keep them in the case file for future reference.

12. Where service is made by SMS, WeChat, or similar means, the service personnel shall record the sending and receiving mobile phone numbers, the sending time, and the name of the served litigation document, take photos of the service content such as SMS or WeChat, and keep them in the case file for future reference.

13. Based on actual circumstances, work mechanisms to improve the quality and efficiency of service may be explored in a targeted manner, and a dedicated service unit or trial and enforcement departments may be designated to effect service. Provided that laws and judicial interpretations are not violated, innovative and effective working methods may be actively explored.

14. Where a mobile communication device can be reached but personal service or service by mail is not possible, except for judgments, rulings, and mediation documents, telephone service may be used. The service personnel shall inform the party of the content of the litigation document, and record the dialed and answered telephone numbers, the call duration, and the content of the served litigation document. The call process shall be recorded to be kept in the case file for future reference.

15. The provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on service by public announcement shall be strictly applied, and management of service by public announcement shall be strengthened to fully protect the litigation rights of the parties. Service by public announcement may be used only when the person on whom service is to be made is whereabouts unknown, or when service cannot be made by other means provided in Chapter 2, Section 7 of Part I of the Civil Procedure Law.

16. In the work of service, the strength of grassroots organizations and social forces may be leveraged, and communication and coordination with grassroots organizations and relevant departments shall be strengthened to create a favorable external environment for service work. Where conditions permit, grassroots organizations may be requested to assist in service, and appropriate fees may be paid.

17. A nationwide court system coordination awareness shall be established. For litigation documents entrusted for service by other courts, service shall be carried out carefully and promptly. Courts are encouraged to establish a collaborative mechanism for entrusted service to reduce service costs and improve service efficiency.
